# Incident Report — STRRAT RAT Infection

**Evidence:** `2024-07-30-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (11,562 frames, 585.7 sec, capture start 2024-07-30 06:38:48 +0400). No IDS/Suricata exports were present in the evidence directory — findings below are derived entirely from packet analysis (tshark/Wireshark).

## Victim host

| Attribute | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | **172.16.1.66** | conversation/DNS traffic |
| MAC | **00:1e:64:ec:f3:08** | Ethernet header |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-SKBR25F** | NBNS name registration, DNS PTR/A queries, Kerberos `desktop-skbr25f$` |
| AD domain | wiresharkworkshop.online (DC: WIRESHARK-WS-DC, 172.16.1.4) | LDAP/Kerberos/CLDAP SRV lookups |
| Logged-in user | **ccollier** | Kerberos AS-REQ `CNameString`, corroborated by malware beacon field `ccollier` |
| OS (self-reported by host) | Microsoft Windows 11 Pro, 64-bit | malware beacon payload |
| Installed AV | Windows Defender | malware beacon payload |

## Malware family

**STRRAT** (Java-based remote access trojan). **Signature-confirmed** — the C2 check-in payload contains the literal, unobfuscated string `STRRAT` as the campaign/protocol tag, e.g. (TCP stream 83, frame 9119 onward):

```
ping|STRRAT|1BE8292C|DESKTOP-SKBR25F|ccollier|Microsoft Windows 11 Pro|64-bit|Windows Defender||1.6|US:United States|Not Installed|1 Sec
```

Bot ID `1BE8292C`, reported STRRAT version `1.6`. This is not inference from behavior — the plaintext protocol string names the family directly. STRRAT's active-window-tracking feature is also present: later beacons carry a base64 field that decodes to the victim's foreground window title, e.g. `SG9tZQ==`→`Home`, `RG9jdW1lbnRz`→`Documents`, `UGljdHVyZXM=`→`Pictures`, `UHJvZ3JhbSBNYW5hZ2Vy`→`Program Manager`, `cG91bmRzLWZvcm11bGEg...`→`pounds-formula [Compatibility Mode] - PowerPoint`, `RmFuYWQg...`→`Fanad Head Lighthouse - Paint` — consistent with the user actively working while the RAT tracks their activity.

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 server (signature-confirmed, unencrypted TCP):**
- `141.98.10.79:12132` — beacon interval ~5 seconds, plaintext pipe-delimited protocol. First contact: frame 9066, t=76.99s (SYN); ongoing through end of capture (last packet t=585.66s, frame 11562) — infection was active for the entire remainder of the capture (~8.5 minutes).
- No DNS query for 141.98.10.79 appears anywhere in the capture — the IP is hardcoded in the malware, a classic C2 trait (also the only remote host in this pcap contacted with no prior name resolution).

**Bot/machine ID:** `1BE8292C`

**Supporting/behavioral indicator — geolocation self-check:**
- `ip-api.com` (resolved to 208.95.112.1) — HTTP GET `/json/` at t=77.87s, spoofed User-Agent `Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) ... Chrome/73.0.3683.86`, response `"country":"United States","countryCode":"US"...`. This occurs between the C2 TCP handshake (76.99s) and the first beacon (78.07s), and the result (`US:United States`) is exactly what appears in the following STRRAT ping — this is the malware's own geo-lookup, not user browsing.

**Probable delivery/staging chain (behavioral, timing-based — payload content is TLS-encrypted and unrecoverable in this capture):**
- `github.com` (140.82.113.3) and `objects.githubusercontent.com` (185.199.108/109/110/111.133) — TLS session at t=64.2–70.8s, ~833 KB transferred from GitHub release-asset infrastructure.
- `repo1.maven.org` (199.232.196.209, 199.232.192.209) — TLS session at t=68.0–73.8s, ~8.9 MB transferred (Maven Central — consistent with a Java runtime pulling dependency JARs, matching STRRAT's Java-based nature).
- ~3–9 seconds after these downloads complete, the STRRAT process launches, performs its geo-IP check (ip-api.com, t=77.87s), and starts C2 beaconing (t=78.07s, first "ping").
- No file names or SHA256 hashes could be extracted — these three sessions are TLS 1.2/1.3 and no keys are available, so only domain/IP/timing evidence is stated here; this portion is **behavioral/circumstantial**, not signature-confirmed.

**No other C2 domains, malicious URLs, or file transfers were found.** All other DNS/TLS activity (MSN, Bing, Office/Outlook, Windows telemetry/WNS, Skype, `javadl-esd-secure.oracle.com`) resolves to legitimate Microsoft/Akamai/Oracle infrastructure and shows normal enterprise-workstation background traffic.

## Summary

Host **DESKTOP-SKBR25F** (172.16.1.66, MAC 00:1e:64:ec:f3:08), logged in as **ccollier**, is infected with **STRRAT** (v1.6, bot ID `1BE8292C`). Around t=64–74s the host pulled content from GitHub and Maven Central (likely the malicious Java payload and its runtime dependencies), then began beaconing to **141.98.10.79:12132** in cleartext every ~5 seconds for the rest of the capture, performing an `ip-api.com` geo-lookup as part of its check-in. Recommend isolating the host, resetting the `ccollier` account, and blocking `141.98.10.79:12132` at the perimeter.
